caption: Receive: the clock from a Send of the same name, arriving at the wave without a wire
why: A value used all over a big graph - the beat, the clock, a master speed - means wires from one node crossing everything to reach the others. Send and Receive carry it without a wire: whatever feeds a Send named clock comes out of every Receive named clock, wherever they sit.
Its neighbours: Knot routes a wire neatly; sub-graphs hide wiring inside a node; Send and Receive remove the wire. Send colour and Receive colour do the same for colours.
steps: A Send named clock carries **Time** times 0.3.
This Receive's **name** is clock, so its `out` is that value: it is the **Wave**'s phase. A second Receive of the same name feeds the palette's scroll.
A Receive whose name no Send has is an error, shown on the node.
When the graph compiles, each Receive is joined to its Send and both vanish.

try.label: Lose the Send
try.text: name ticks: no Send has that name - the node says so, and the build waits until it matches again.
